full_dataset_size: Committed: 3 CSVs, 113 MB total (IWB 20220621 14.0 MB, IWB 20220823 5.8 MB, IWV 20220516 93.6 MB, ~600k rows combined). What the scraper would produce: month-end (and daily for recent years) holdings for 395 iShares ETFs back to 2006; IWV alone is ~3,000 rows per snapshot, so a full monthly IWV history is roughly 200 snapshots x 3k = 0.6M rows / ~100 MB; the whole product line would be several GB.
description: Per-holding, per-snapshot constituent files for iShares ETFs (weight, share count, market value, price, sector, CUSIP/ISIN/SEDOL), produced by a scraper of ishares.com's holdings-history download; the committed snapshots cover the Russell 1000 ETF (IWB) month-ends Dec 2019-Jul 2022 and the head of a 2006+ Russell 3000 (IWV) history. Grain is fund x as_of_date x security. For ABNB an analyst would build a point-in-time series of ABNB's index weight and shares held by passive funds (IWB/IWV, plus travel or consumer-discretionary sector ETFs) as a passive-ownership and index-flow proxy, and the same for BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT (all 32 snapshots in IWB). ABNB only enters IWB in the 2022-06-30 snapshot, so the committed data give just two ABNB observations; anything longer requires running the scraper.
issues: No licence declared on the repo (all rights reserved by default) and the underlying data belong to BlackRock/iShares under its site terms - a human must decide before the scraper is run or the data redistributed; the scraper (sync_etf_downloader.py / easy_downloader.py) was NOT run. ABNB appears in only 2 of the 32 committed IWB snapshots (Jun and Jul 2022), so the committed data are near-useless for ABNB on their own; the value is the method. ishares.com download URLs may have changed since the last push (2024-10-28), so the scraper may need repair. The IWV file was truncated to its first 2 MB (2006-07 rows only) to stay under the size cap. Optional S3/Athena path needs AWS credentials; not used.
